abstract: A total of 180 consecutive testicular cancers containing a component of embryonal carcinoma (EC) were reviewed to assess the morphologic features of the EC component. EC mostly (84%) occurred as a component of a mixed germ cell tumor, but 16% were pure. Solid (55%), glandular (17%), and papillary (11%) were the most common primary patterns (predominant architectural pattern occupying at least 50%), whereas other less common primary patterns included nested (3%), micropapillary (2%), anastomosing glandular (1%), sieve-like glandular (<1%), pseudopapillary (<1%), and blastocyst-like (<1%). Occasionally, EC developed predominantly in the context of polyembryoma-like (6%) and diffuse embryoma-like ("necklace" pattern) (3%) proliferations. In all, 69% had secondary architectural patterns, the most frequent being glandular (31%), papillary (14%), and solid (12%). An appliqué appearance, in which smudged and degenerate-appearing EC cells appear "applied" to the tumor periphery, was common (67%). EC cells with clear cytoplasm and distinct cell membranes (seminoma-like) were present in 11%, and dense lymphocytic infiltration and granulomatous inflammation were seen in 7% and 3%, respectively. Features simulating yolk sac tumor and teratoma were also seen: pseudoendodermal sinuses (34%), columnar cells (20%), and secretory-type subnuclear cytoplasmic vacuoles (6%). Syncytiotrophoblast cells were frequent (46%). Intratubular EC, typically partly necrotic and calcified, occurred in 24%. The associated stroma was more often non-neoplastic (53%) than neoplastic (29%). The rarity of some poorly characterized patterns of EC (micropapillary, blastocyst-like, anastomosing glandular, and sieve-like glandular) and some that overlap with those of other germ cell tumors, as well as some uncommon cytologic features, may result in misinterpretation, potentially impacting management. The association with other more common patterns and typical cytologic features, together with simple awareness of these variant morphologies, are helpful in establishing an accurate diagnosis of EC.
abstract_ja: 胎児性癌(EC)成分を含む精巣がん連続180例を対象に、EC成分の形態学的特徴を検討した。ECは84%が混合型胚細胞腫瘍の一成分として出現し、16%は単独型であった。主要な一次構築パターンは充実型(55%)、腺型(17%)、乳頭型(11%)が最も多く、そのほかに巣状(3%)、微小乳頭状(2%)、吻合腺型(1%)、篩状腺型(<1%)、偽乳頭状(<1%)、胞胚様(<1%)などの比較的まれなパターンがみられた。ときに多胚腫様(6%)やびまん性胚腫様(「ネックレス」パターン)(3%)の増殖を背景としてECが優勢に出現することもあった。全体の69%には二次的構築パターンがみられ、最も多いのは腺型(31%)、乳頭型(14%)、充実型(12%)であった。腫瘍辺縁にEC細胞が汚れて変性したような像で「貼り付けられた」ように見える所見(アップリケ様外観)が67%と高頻度にみられた。明るい細胞質と明瞭な細胞膜を持つEC細胞(セミノーマ様)が11%、高度のリンパ球浸潤が7%、肉芽腫性炎症が3%にみられた。卵黄嚢腫瘍や奇形腫を模倣する所見も認められ、偽内胚葉洞(34%)、円柱状細胞(20%)、分泌型の核下細胞質空胞(6%)がみられた。合胞体栄養膜細胞は46%で多数認められた。精細管内ECは、典型的には部分的に壊死・石灰化しており、24%にみられた。随伴する間質は、腫瘍性よりも非腫瘍性であることが多かった(53%対29%)。一部の十分に特徴づけられていないECパターン(微小乳頭状、胞胚様、吻合腺型、篩状腺型)や、他の胚細胞腫瘍の所見と重なるパターン、さらにまれな細胞学的特徴は、誤診を招きうる。これは治療方針に影響を与える可能性がある。より一般的なパターンや典型的な細胞学的特徴との関連性、そしてこれらの変異形態を認識することは、ECの正確な診断に役立つ。
